Can we simplify these macros a little?  They have a level of obfuscation that isn't great... and frankly I'm having trouble reading them.

I get these deduplicate some patterns, which is great, but not being able to trace field -> code that generates it is hard.

ack. separating to CAP_FIELD and CAP_FIELD_HEX, etc..

didn't know my comments were draft

@ed@tanous.net - Should we do something with these like save them in `xxd` format and reverse-xxd them during test cases?  These probably won't change often, I understand, but pretty impossible to review them if they do.
seems like a good idea.  is that something you want to make a patch for?  if not I can see if Aushim wants to do it.
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libcper/+/78688
I think it's a good idea.  I've been using XXD for debugging in this project to manually check the CPER extraction and diffs.
Why did we change a number of fields that are unrelated to the new feature being added?
I don't get this comment which field?  The recordlength did pretty much double because I added hex for everything.

The device capabilities register breaks down into smaller fields than this.  Lets decode these into as close to human readable fields as possible.

For example, this field would be

device_capabilies: {
   maximum_payload_size: 1,
   extended_tags_supported: true,
   acceptable_los_latency: 3
   ....
}

I suspect that will remove the need to have both hex and int decodes for a lot of the fields.

latest push does this.  All registers has been decoded.
That about 300+ registers/fields.
I've purposely left blank fields of length 1, because we needed to go through each of them to determine if they are boolean or require some sort of dictionary/decode.

fields like aer error severity, a boolean of True/False doesn't make sense as a simple example.

The sort order on these is a little awkward.  I can't tell if that's just how you build this file, and these just need sorted, or if that's how they show up in the json file itself.  We probably want the hex decode next to the int decode.
postfix changed from "_2" to just "2", no more hex fields.
I suspect when you add more structure to this, this list will drop considerably.
It'll drop exactly in half for the PCIe capabilities.  More registers will need to be added for the AER section, once we decide what to do with the TLP Header Registers.
This list is for when fields are mutually exclusive.  In unit tests, we should be generating records with every field set.

I think that's smart.  We would need to update the unit test to generate and test different data.  Gen-section-pcie.c would need to make sure to set certain bits to trigger the mutual exclusive data.

pcie_capabilities.capability_version 
advanced_error_capabilities_and_control.logged_tlp_was_flit_mode

this push won't add this tough as it's already getting really long.
Plus for this push I've not added things like TLP Header.

copied from IM discussion.
Treat the .h file like a structured spec for other people and scripts to use.  We're following the rules IP vs what makes more sense for coding.

The UINT16 is because this is a UINT16 register (size 2).  A strict PCIe implementation would return an error if you tried to do a size 1 read to this size 2 register.
